## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ambajātaka* (Ja 474) is a birth story in the Pali Jātaka collection. According to the frame narrative set at Jetavana, the Buddha told this story concerning Devadatta, who had repudiated his teacher, caused a schism in the Saṅgha, and subsequently fell into the Avīci hell. In the conclusion (*samodhāna*) of the past story, the Buddha connects the narrative to the present, explaining that Devadatta had likewise repudiated his teacher in a past life and met with great ruin as an ungrateful pupil (*akataññū māṇavo*), while Ānanda was the king and the Bodhisatta was a *caṇḍālaputta* [Fausböll 1887].
